title: SAMPLE — Weekly outlook: spillover risk steady at rung 3; EU misses sanctions deadline
bottom_line: The ladder holds at rung 3 for a third week, driven by drone incursions in Poland and Moldova and debris in Romania. Belarus ended its snap readiness check near Grodno on schedule. Ukraine struck an ammunition depot near Klintsy, which the Bryansk governor acknowledged. EU leaders missed their 25 October target for the 20th sanctions package. The 6-to-12-month risk of a deliberate Russian attack on NATO stays highly unlikely (10%).

ladder.rationale: Rung 3 since 5 October from incursions in Poland and Moldova and debris in Romania; no deaths or deliberate strikes on European territory.

developments.headline: Belarus ends snap readiness check near Grodno
developments.summary: Belarus's defence ministry said the snap check of about 3,000 troops near Grodno ended on schedule and units returned to their garrisons. Lithuanian officials said they saw no movement toward the border during the exercise.

developments.headline: Ukraine strikes ammunition depot near Klintsy in Bryansk Oblast
developments.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said drones hit an ammunition depot near Klintsy, about 60 km from the border. The Bryansk governor reported a drone attack on the district and a fire at a military site.
developments.russian_framing: The governor said air defences shot down most of the drones (claim).

developments.headline: EU leaders miss their 25 October deadline for the 20th sanctions package
developments.summary: EU leaders ended their summit without adopting the 20th sanctions package after Hungary and Slovakia sought energy exemptions. Diplomats expect a new attempt in November.
developments.russian_framing: TASS said the delay showed European unity was fraying (claim).

categories.text: ISW reports slow Russian gains near Pokrovsk with no sign of operational breakthrough.
Klintsy depot strike (d2), acknowledged by the Bryansk governor.

judgement.text:
We assess that spillover risk is steady. The ladder has been at rung 3 for three weeks because of stray drones and debris from Russian strikes near the Polish, Moldovan and Romanian borders, not because of deliberate action. The Belarusian snap check near Grodno was the week's main posture signal; it ended on schedule and Lithuanian monitoring saw no movement toward the border, so the military-pressure pathway stays remote (5%).

The missed sanctions deadline matters more for cohesion than for incidents. Hungary and Slovakia used the package to seek energy exemptions, as they did with earlier packages, and both eventually signed. We expect adoption in November, but the delay keeps shadow-fleet tankers off the list for longer, which bears on the maritime pathway in the Baltic.

Ukraine's strikes inside Russia continue at about four a week, and Russia has not answered them with steps against European suppliers beyond rhetoric. We keep the 30-day odds of a deadly or deliberate incident at highly unlikely (15%).
judgement.change_my_mind: A Russian unit moving from Ukraine toward Finland or the Baltics, or a sabotage attack causing deaths, would raise the medium-term outlook.

forecasts_new.question: Will the EU adopt its 20th sanctions package against Russia by 30 November 2026?
forecasts_new.resolution_criteria: The Council of the EU announces adoption of the 20th package on or before 30 November 2026.
forecasts_new.base_rate_note: Earlier packages blocked at a summit were usually adopted within five weeks.

forecast_resolutions.note: EU leaders ended the summit without adopting the 20th package.

taiwan: The sanctions delay shows how a single member state can slow the EU's response to Russia, a precedent Beijing watches when it weighs Europe's likely reaction to pressure on Taiwan. Ukraine's steady deep-strike campaign also keeps European interceptor stocks tight, which delays deliveries Taiwan is waiting for.

medium_term.question: Will Russia conduct a deliberate, attributable armed attack on NATO territory in the next 12 months?
medium_term.text: We assess a deliberate attack in the next year as highly unlikely (10%). Russia's main force remains committed in Ukraine, and the Estonian service's latest briefing describes rebuilding in the Leningrad Military District as early-stage. The risk would rise quickly after a ceasefire that freed forces, which is why we track redeployment and mobilisation as strategic indicators. Today none of them is active.

long_term.question: Will Russia and a NATO member be in direct armed conflict by the end of 2030?
long_term.text: Several European services judge that Russia could be ready for a limited war with NATO within three to five years of a ceasefire. We weigh that capability estimate against intent, US commitment and European rearmament, and assess direct conflict by 2030 as highly unlikely (20%), with low confidence because the main drivers are political.
